correctness.rationale: Using the 48 canonical Fermat quartic lines partitioned into three 16-line pairings, solving coordinate equations gives precise same-family row-or-column and mixed-family modular incidence rules. Independently rebuilt the 48x48 symmetric integer adjacency matrix from those congruences; obtained all degrees 14 and 336 edges, exact characteristic polynomial (t-14)(t-2)^28(t+2)^12(t+6)^6(t+10), and counted every nonedge common-neighbor entry (A^2)ij: 96 at 2, 192 at 4, 480 at 6, 24 at 10, total 792. On the smooth quartic each line has self-intersection -2, thus Gram=A-2I; its eigenvalues yield rank20 inertia (1,19,28). The calculation is exhaustive for the finite complete 48-line set (assuming the classical complete line listing), not an infinite extrapolation.
